prompt: What does Eventarc deliver to a destination, whatever the source?
hint: One format for everything.

choices.text: A Pub/Sub message the destination must pull
choices.why: Delivery is a push; the destination pulls nothing.

choices.text: A row in a table the destination reads
choices.why: Nothing is written to a table for the destination.

choices.text: A CloudEvent over HTTP
choices.why: Right. Every source arrives in the same shape.

choices.text: An audit log entry, for every kind of source
choices.why: Audit entries are one source among several.

prompt: Match each part of a trigger to the question it answers.
hint: Three answers and an identity.

prompt: The plan of the photos trigger printed transport (known after apply). Why?
hint: Who makes the topic?

choices.text: Eventarc makes and names them itself
choices.why: Right. They exist only once the trigger does.

choices.text: The file left out a transport block it needs
choices.why: A trigger on a Google source needs none; Eventarc makes it.

choices.text: The token no-account could not read the topic
choices.why: Nothing was read; the plan asked no API.

choices.text: Storage triggers have no transport at all
choices.why: They travel through Pub/Sub like most sources.

prompt: A team applies the photos trigger and no event ever arrives, though uploads succeed. The plan was clean. Which cause does the lesson name?
hint: What can a plan not see?

choices.text: The function returned normally, so Eventarc stopped delivering
choices.why: A normal return is success; delivery continues.

choices.text: Storage events need audit logs turned on first
choices.why: Storage events are direct; audit logs are another source.

choices.text: The event type was misspelt, and Terraform accepted it silently
choices.why: Possible in general, but here the file matched the documented type.

choices.text: The bucket's agent lacks the Pub/Sub publish grant
choices.why: Right. A one-time grant per project, invisible to a plan.

prompt: A trigger on a bucket in São Paulo is created in the region ___.
hint: The bucket's own region.

prompt: Which two ways does Cloud Storage have of announcing a change?
hint: One old, one new.

choices.text: An email to the project owner, and a webhook
choices.why: Neither; both ways go through events.

choices.text: Pub/Sub notifications and Eventarc
choices.why: Right. The metadata is the same JSON in both.

choices.text: An audit log entry, and a polling API
choices.why: Audit logs are a fallback for services with no direct events.

choices.text: A file written next to the object, and a Pub/Sub notification
choices.why: No file is written beside the object.

prompt: Why does the lab use curl to upload to fake-gcs-server rather than gcloud storage cp?
hint: The same reason as in lesson 17.

choices.text: gcloud storage cannot send image files
choices.why: It sends any file; the account is the obstacle.

choices.text: curl is faster for large files
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: gcloud demands an account
choices.why: Right. curl speaks the JSON API with no credentials.

choices.text: fake-gcs-server only accepts multipart uploads, which gcloud does not send
choices.why: It accepted a simple media upload from curl.

prompt: The function printed OBJECT_FINALIZE and OBJECT_DELETE without decoding the data. Where did it read them?
hint: A summary travels beside the data.

choices.text: In the message's attributes, under eventType
choices.why: Right. Bucket and object are there too.

choices.text: In the CloudEvent's ce-type header
choices.why: The type there is messagePublished, the Pub/Sub one.

choices.text: In the URL the push subscription called
choices.why: The URL was the same for both.

choices.text: In the object's content type
choices.why: That is image/jpeg for both.

prompt: The uploaded photo was made with head -c 48213 /dev/urandom. What size, in bytes, did the finalize event report?
hint: -c counts bytes.

prompt: The shop moves from a Pub/Sub notification to an Eventarc storage trigger. Which part of the thumbnails code must change?
hint: The envelope differs; the metadata does not.

choices.text: The thumbnail work, because the object JSON changes
choices.why: The metadata is the same JSON.

choices.text: Nothing, the two deliveries are byte for byte the same
choices.why: There is no message to unwrap in the direct event.

choices.text: The decorator, which must become http
choices.why: Both arrive as CloudEvents.

choices.text: The parsing, since there is no message to unwrap
choices.why: Right. Keep parsing and work in separate functions.

prompt: The number in an object's metadata that tells two versions of the same name apart is its ___.
hint: It counts writes to that name.

prompt: When does Eventarc need Cloud Audit Logs to see a change?
hint: Not every service announces its own.

choices.text: For every event, as the transport
choices.why: The transport is Pub/Sub.

choices.text: When the service announces nothing directly
choices.why: Right. Audit entries are the widest net.

choices.text: Only for Cloud Storage uploads
choices.why: Storage has direct events.

choices.text: When the destination is a function rather than a service
choices.why: The destination does not decide the source.

prompt: Match each criterion of the new-machines trigger to its value.
hint: Type, service, method.

prompt: A trigger on storage.objects.get through audit logs never fires. What is the likely cause?
hint: Reading data is a different kind of log.

choices.text: Audit triggers fire only for deletions
choices.why: They fire for any logged method.

choices.text: get is a read, and Eventarc ignores reads
choices.why: Eventarc matches what is logged; the log is the gap.

choices.text: Data access logs are off unless turned on for that service
choices.why: Right. A method that is not logged never fires, and nothing says so.

choices.text: The method name needs a v1 prefix
choices.why: Naming is not the reason here.

prompt: Why is an audit-log trigger wrong for sending a customer their receipt?
hint: Who is waiting, and for how long?

choices.text: Delivery takes up to minutes, and a person is waiting
choices.why: Right. Fine for inventory, wrong for anything awaited.

choices.text: Audit entries are deleted after one hour
choices.why: Retention is not the issue.

choices.text: Audit triggers cannot reach Cloud Run
choices.why: The destination can be Cloud Run.

choices.text: Receipts are personal data, which audit logs refuse
choices.why: The trigger carries the API call, not the receipt.

prompt: A trigger in southamerica-east1 on a global service's audit entries sees nothing. Why?
hint: Where are the entries written?

choices.text: Global services write no audit entries
choices.why: They do, globally.

choices.text: São Paulo does not offer Eventarc for audit logs of any kind
choices.why: The storage trigger lived there.

choices.text: The service account lacks the logging role
choices.why: A permission gap is possible, but location is the stated cause.

choices.text: Entries are written globally; the trigger must be too
choices.why: Right. The location has to match where the entries land.

prompt: How many times do Eventarc and Pub/Sub promise to deliver an event?
hint: Read the section's first bold sentence.

choices.text: Exactly once
choices.why: That is the comfortable assumption the lesson corrects.

choices.text: At least once
choices.why: Right. A duplicate can arrive even when nothing failed.

choices.text: At most once
choices.why: Lost events are not the promise; repeated ones are.

choices.text: Once per subscriber and region
choices.why: There is no such count.

prompt: The flaky function received message 1 how many times in the ten seconds the lab waited?
hint: grep -c counted them.

prompt: Why can a duplicate arrive even when the function succeeded?
hint: Something travels back after the work.

choices.text: Pub/Sub sends every message twice for safety
choices.why: Not by design; by a lost acknowledgement.

choices.text: The framework calls the function twice per request
choices.why: One request, one call.

choices.text: The acknowledgement got lost on the way back
choices.why: Right. The sender then delivers again.

choices.text: Two triggers are always created per function
choices.why: One trigger per deployment.

prompt: Order what happens to a message whose function always fails, on a subscription with a dead-letter topic and 5 attempts.
hint: The dead-letter topic comes after the last attempt.
items: The message is pushed and the function raises
Pub/Sub waits, longer each time, and pushes again
The message moves to the dead-letter topic

prompt: Which of these is idempotent by nature?
hint: Doing it twice leaves the world as once did.

choices.text: Writing a thumbnail to a fixed file name
choices.why: Right. The same file twice is the same file.

choices.text: Sending an order confirmation email
choices.why: Twice is two emails.

choices.text: Adding the order total to a monthly sum
choices.why: Twice adds it twice.

choices.text: Charging the customer's card
choices.why: Twice is two charges.

prompt: An event arrives with malformed data. What should the function do, by this lesson?
hint: Will retrying help?

choices.text: Raise, so that it is retried until fixed
choices.why: It will be malformed on every attempt.

choices.text: Sleep a minute, then raise
choices.why: Waiting does not fix the data.

choices.text: Delete the subscription
choices.why: That stops every event, good ones too.

choices.text: Log it and return normally
choices.why: Right. Raising would only buy a day of identical failures.

prompt: A topic that receives messages after their last failed attempt is called a ___-letter topic.
hint: Where undeliverable post goes.

prompt: A function is deployed with an event trigger and retries left at their default. Which statements are true? Choose all that apply.
hint: What is the default?

choices.text: A failed event is dropped after one attempt
choices.why: Right; retries are off by default.

choices.text: A failure can be lost without anyone noticing
choices.why: Right; off, a failure is lost quietly.

choices.text: Each event is retried for 24 hours
choices.why: Only with retries turned on.

choices.text: Duplicates become impossible
choices.why: A lost acknowledgement still causes one.
